Coming from another tool

Familiar generation settings, supported features, and what changes when a volunteer worker runs the model.

Short read8 parts

What this covers

Explanation detail

  1. 1 · Studio settings

    Many controls will be familiar: , , , , , and . controls the amount of change in img2img. and its denoising control are in Size. is in Sampling and is set per request.The reference explains each setting. Supported options and defaults can differ from your previous tool, so compare them before reusing a saved configuration.
    Size · Interactive explorer Hires fix
    Hires fix Off
    Hires fix On
    Result comparison 768 × 1536

    Generated in one pass at the full requested size. Past the model's comfortable size, this can duplicate details, stretch anatomy, or split one subject into several.Generated smaller first, then enlarged and redrawn. The first pass decides the composition, so the final image is more likely to stay coherent.

    When you ask for more pixels than a model comfortably generates in one pass, it may repeat subjects or stretch shapes instead of making a larger coherent scene. Hires-fix composes a smaller image first, then enlarges it and redraws detail at the requested size.

    Fetching the example images.

    Sampling · Interactive explorer CLIP skip
    CLIP skip 2 512 × 512

    Skips the last layer. On an anime-lineage model this is the intended setting; elsewhere it just loosens the prompt.

    How many layers to cut from the end of the text encoder. Anime-lineage models were trained expecting one to be cut.

    1Drag to compare3

    Fetching the example images.

  2. 2 · Remote generation

    The image model runs on a volunteer's . Your browser prepares the request and sends it to .You do not need to download model files. The studio shows queue and generation status; timing depends on the worker that accepts the job.

  3. 3 · Kudos and request limits

    reflect contributions and generation use. They influence queue priority, and some requests require an upfront balance.Generation is free, including anonymous use, subject to request limits. Allow downgrade can reduce supported settings when a request does not meet kudos requirements.

  4. 4 · Model availability

    lists models offered through the Horde. Workers choose which to load, so availability changes.Check the worker count before sending a request. A model with no compatible worker may remain queued and expire.

  5. 5 · Suggested settings

    The model reference can supply suggested sampler, , and values. The studio shows these with the relevant controls.Use them as starting points. A missing suggestion does not mean every value is suitable.

  6. 6 · Reproducibility

    Keep and the other settings fixed for useful comparisons.Worker hardware, software versions, and model files can differ. Matching a saved seed and settings therefore does not guarantee an identical image.
    Sampling · Interactive explorer Seed
    Seed Seed A 1024 × 1024

    One draw of this prompt. Every other strip in this library holds this seed.

    The seed picks which image you get, not how good it is. The same seed with the same settings gives you the same picture again, which is what makes a result worth writing down; change it and you get another draw of the same prompt.

    Seed ADrag to compareSeed F

    Fetching the example images.

  7. 7 · Supported features

    The studio offers features supported by the Horde API and compatible workers. It cannot run arbitrary extension scripts or custom workflows from another application.Supported options can depend on the model and worker version. Check the studio's compatibility messages.Workers manage model files. Your browser stores studio settings and results, so local storage still matters for keeping your images.

  8. 8 · First request

    Follow the first-image tutorial to make a request with familiar controls.It shows how to choose a model, set the generation options, and send the job. Skip steps you already know, then compare the result with the example.
